findings.title: Public findMany method removed, breaking existing callers
findings.body: The diff removes `InsightsBookingService.findMany` and replaces it with `getBaseConditions`, which only returns a raw SQL fragment. Any code that currently calls `service.findMany(...)` will fail to compile or throw at runtime. Since the PR only updates the service and its tests, callers need to be updated or a compatible query method needs to remain.

findings.title: Org scope skips org memberships when there are no child teams
findings.body: `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` always includes `orgId` in `teamIds`, but it only fetches memberships when `teamsFromOrg.length > 0`. For an organization that has direct members but no child teams, `userIdsFromOrg` becomes empty, so the generated condition omits the `userId = ANY(...) AND "isTeamBooking" = false` branch and excludes non-team bookings for org members. Fetch memberships for `teamIds` unconditionally.

findings.title: SQL fragment assertions depend on array order and internal representation
findings.body: The org-scope test compares the returned `Prisma.Sql` fragment with a literal fragment containing exact `teamIds` and `userIds` arrays. The service builds those arrays from repository queries that do not show explicit ordering, and it composes fragments with `reduce`. If rows are returned in a different order, or if Prisma represents composed fragments differently, the test can fail even though the SQL condition is semantically correct. Normalize the SQL text/values or sort/compare IDs unordered.

findings.title: Condition caching can trigger duplicate concurrent DB queries
findings.body: `getAuthorizationConditions` checks `this.cachedAuthConditions === undefined` and then awaits `buildAuthorizationConditions()`. If multiple callers invoke it before the first build completes, all see the cache as undefined and issue duplicate membership/team queries. Cache the in-flight promise if this service can be called concurrently.
